grades.reason: Discusses TLB hierarchy and page table loading. It says nothing about cacheable versus device/uncached memory attributes.

grades.quote: The RISC-V Privileged ISA defines Physical Memory Attributes (PMAs) which specify, among other things, whether portions of the address space are coherent and/or cacheable.
grades.reason: Names the RISC-V Physical Memory Attributes that separate cacheable main memory from I/O regions: main memory vs I/O, cacheability, coherence, and idempotency (side effects). It frames them by their relation to the memory model and does not fully lay out the distinction.

grades.quote: In any case, the definition of the control value for the memory access type is always the same: `0` for strongly-ordered uncached, `1` for coherent cached, `2` for weakly-ordered uncached, and `3` for reserved.
grades.reason: Directly describes LoongArch memory access types: coherent cached (CC) vs strongly-ordered uncached (SUC) and weakly-ordered uncached (WUC). It also says how the type is selected, by CSR.CRMD.DATF/DATM, by the direct-mapping window MAT field, or by the page-table-entry MAT field.
Covers the LoongArch weak consistency model and synchronization instructions. It does not distinguish cacheable memory from device-style accesses.
